stories.title: Queens’ Tallest Tower Reaches 90% Leased, Adds First Retail Tenants
stories.excerpt: BLDG Management Co., Inc announced that The Orchard, Queens’ tallest tower, has surpassed 90% leased across its 824 residences nine months after launching residential leasing. The milestone occurs as the 70-story Long Island City development recently signed its first three retail tenants: K-beauty brand Tokimo, Japanese tea and beverage brand Mollytea and financial technology platform Intuit. Together, the three tenants have leased more than 7,468 square feet, with limited retail space remaining. All tenants will make their Long Island City debut and are expected to open in 2027. “The Orchard was designed to be more than a place to live, with residences, amenities and services that give people opportunities to live, work and connect right at home,” said Lloyd Goldman, president of BLDG Management. “BLDG has been part of the Long Island City community for more than 60 years, and we wanted The Orchard to build on that legacy by creating a place that serves both residents and the broader neighborhood. Surpassing 90% leased in just nine months reflects the demand for what we’ve created, while the addition of Tokimo, Mollytea, and Intuit will make The Orchard an even more dynamic destination for residents and the LIC community.” The post Queens’ Tallest Tower Reaches 90% Leased, Adds First Retail Tenants appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: The Orchard, Long Island City: 824-unit tower 90% leased in 9 months post-launch.
K-beauty, tea, fintech retail tenants signed 7,468 sq ft; openings slated 2027.
Strong lease-up velocity signals robust demand for mixed-use residential in Queens submarkets.
stories.summary: BLDG Management's The Orchard in Long Island City has leased 90% of its 824 apartments within nine months of opening, with three inaugural retail tenants—Tokimo, Mollytea, and Intuit—committing to over 7,468 square feet of space, set to open in 2027. The rapid absorption and retail anchor signings underscore sustained demand for premium residential in the submarket. The addition of experiential and financial-services tenants reflects broader neighborhood densification and institutional tenant interest.
stories.impact: Long Island City's absorption velocity and mixed-use retail anchoring (especially fintech) signal strengthening residential fundamentals and neighborhood maturation, raising the bar for competing multifamily entrants. This validates the viability of higher-density, amenity-rich development and may accelerate rent growth expectations—important for new project underwriting and competitive positioning in the Queens market.

stories.title: Gencom-Led JV Buys InterContinental in Downtown Miami for $300M
stories.excerpt: Gencom and White Bridge Capital bought the waterfront InterContinental Miami hotel, paying about $300 million, Bloomberg reported. The 34-story property features 652 rooms at 100 Chopin Plaza, facing Biscayne Bay, right off of Biscayne Boulevard, sitting just south of the Brickell district. The 465,000-square-foot building was constructed in 1983, and it houses about 90,000 square feet of indoor and outdoor event space and a rooftop pool. The seller — China’s Dajia Insurance Group, which has owned the asset since 2005 — recently renovated the property. “The InterContinental Miami’s significant recent capital investment, strong operating performance and diversified mix of leisure, corporate and group business provide a solid foundation for long-term value creation to Gencom and its investors,” Ignasi Puig, managing director of acquisitions at Gencom, said in a statement. Other recent hospitality acquisitions in the area include Blackstone’s purchase of the 352-room East hotel last year. Gencom’s acquisition comes nearly a year after the Miami-based firm purchased the InterContinental New York Times Square for $230 million. In the Miami area, it owns the Ritz-Carlton hotels in Coconut Grove and Key Biscayne, the latter of which reopened last year after a $100 million renovation. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Gencom, White Bridge Capital buy InterContinental Miami waterfront hotel for ~$300M.
34-story, 652-room asset in Brickell sits on Biscayne Bay with 90k sq ft event space.
Recent capital investment and group-business diversification cited as foundation for value creation.
stories.summary: Gencom and White Bridge Capital acquired the 652-room InterContinental Miami, a waterfront Brickell property, for approximately $300 million from China's Dajia Insurance Group. The 1983-built, recently renovated asset features significant event and leisure space. The buyers highlighted strong operating performance and diversified revenue streams—leisure, corporate, group business—as value drivers. The deal reflects continued hospitality capital activity in Miami's waterfront submarkets.
stories.impact: While primarily a hospitality transaction, this signals confidence in Miami's economic recovery and tourism/event demand, which can indirectly support multifamily fundamentals (higher employment, visitor-driven service-sector job growth, and ancillary commercial vitality in Brickell). However, it does not directly impact apartment supply or demand; minimal relevance to multifamily development strategy unless your team is considering nearby residential conversion or ground-up projects in the Miami submarket.

stories.title: Immersive Museum Will Make U.S. Debut at OCVIBE
stories.excerpt: teamLab, an art collective known for creating immersive environments, will open its first permanent museum in the U.S. at OCVIBE, the 100-acre sports, entertainment, and arts district currently under construction in Anaheim. Spanning approximately 110,000 square feet, the purpose-built museum will be designed around teamLab’s immersive art experience, with architecture by smith-clementi. A timeline for opening was not announced. The teamLab museum will be an integral part of OCVIBE’s master plan, joining a deliberately curated mix of entertainment, dining, hospitality, and public spaces. Rather than treating art as an amenity, OCVIBE is making it central to the district’s experience, according to the development team. “Bringing teamLab to OCVIBE reflects the importance we’ve placed on integrating arts and culture into the district’s master plan,” said Dan Young, Executive Director of Development at OCVIBE. “It adds an entirely new dimension to what people can experience here in Anaheim, while helping establish OCVIBE as a cultural destination for California and the U.S.” The post Immersive Museum Will Make U.S. Debut at OCVIBE appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: teamLab immersive art museum to occupy 110k sq ft at OCVIBE, Anaheim 100-acre development.
First permanent U.S. location for Tokyo-based art collective; designed by smith-clementi.
Arts/culture integration into master plan positions OCVIBE as regional entertainment destination.
stories.summary: TeamLab, the Tokyo-based immersive art collective, will open its first permanent U.S. museum at OCVIBE, Anaheim's 100-acre sports, entertainment, and arts district under construction, occupying approximately 110,000 square feet. The purpose-built venue is central to OCVIBE's master plan, which emphasizes arts and culture as core attractions alongside hospitality and dining. No opening timeline was announced.
stories.impact: Entertainment district anchoring with arts/culture programming typically generates spillover demand for residential (young professionals, creatives, tourism workers) and can justify higher rents in adjacent or nearby multifamily projects. If Trammell Crow is evaluating residential development within or adjacent to OCVIBE, this confirms the master plan's institutional maturity and the viability of lifestyle-oriented apartment positioning. Monitor the museum's opening timeline and ancillary job growth in Anaheim's service sector.

stories.title: 80-Unit Seniors Housing Development Opens in Suburban Chicago
stories.excerpt: Leyden Senior Apartments, a new four-story independent senior living development in Franklin Park, recently opened. Located at 2506 N. Mannheim Road, Leyden Senior Apartments offers one- and two-bedroom residences. The adjacent newly constructed Carl Fiorito Senior Center will be available to the entire community. Owned by Leyden Apartments LP, Leyden Senior Apartments was designed by Weese Langley Klein Architects with accessible floor plans, energy-efficient appliances and on-site amenities. Evergreen Real Estate Group served as developer for the apartments and the Senior Center and is handling leasing and property management for the community. F.H. Paschen managed construction from start to finish. Funding partners include the Illinois Housing Development Authority, Bank of America, KeyBanc Capital Markets, Hudson Housing Capital, Leyden Township and the Cook County Department of Planning and Development. Mesirow Financial participated in the underwriting syndicate for the IHDA financing and served as lead underwriter for Leyden Township’s general obligation bond offering. The post 80-Unit Seniors Housing Development Opens in Suburban Chicago appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Leyden Senior Apartments, 80-unit independent living facility opened in Franklin Park, suburban Chicago.
Illinois Housing Development Authority, Bank of America, KeyBanc among funding partners.
Evergreen Real Estate Group developed and managing; Carl Fiorito Senior Center adjacent.
stories.summary: Leyden Senior Apartments, an 80-unit independent senior living community, opened in Franklin Park, Illinois, on Mannheim Road. The four-story property, developed by Evergreen Real Estate Group, features accessible one- and two-bedroom floor plans and is supported by IHDA financing alongside Bank of America and KeyBanc Capital Markets. An adjacent senior center serves the broader community. The project signals strong nonprofit and public-sector appetite for senior housing in the Chicago suburbs.
stories.impact: Senior housing development with IHDA and public funding dominates the Chicago suburban market, reducing competitive pressure on market-rate, for-profit multifamily. However, the project's success and funding depth may signal aging-in-place demand and affordability-focus in exurban markets, which could attract alternative capital to senior-designated or mixed-age inclusionary units in future Trammell Crow projects. Limited direct impact on core market-rate multifamily unless you're considering age-restricted or mixed-income strategies in suburban Chicago.

stories.title: Woodcliff Lake Retail Center Trades for $109M in Move from Legacy Ownership
stories.excerpt: David Adam Realty and Cushman & Wakefield closed the $109.5-million sale of Tice’s Corner, the Apple-anchored lifestyle retail destination located at 441 Chestnut Ridge Rd. in Woodcliff Lake, NJ. The sale was among one of New Jersey’s largest single-asset retail transactions of the past decade. Located in one of Bergen County’s most affluent and supply-constrained markets, Tice’s Corner is anchored by Apple and features a curated mix of leading national lifestyle brands including Pottery Barn, Anthropologie and Free People, combining an established, high-performing tenant mix with significant long-term growth potential. Cushman & Wakefield’s Joanna R. Manfro, Managing Director of Northeast Retail, represented the buyer, WS Development. The seller, WS Tice’s Inc., was represented by David Waldman, president of David Adam Realty. “Tice’s Corner is a generational retail asset that had been held by the same legacy ownership for decades,” said Manfro. “When the opportunity for new ownership surfaced, it was a highly competitive process that came together within days, without the asset ever becoming broadly marketed.”. The post Woodcliff Lake Retail Center Trades for $109M in Move from Legacy Ownership appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Tice's Corner, Apple-anchored retail center in Woodcliff Lake, NJ sold for $109.5M.
WS Development acquired from legacy ownership; first major transaction in decades.
Bergen County, supply-constrained, affluent market; portfolio includes Pottery Barn, Anthropologie.
stories.summary: David Adam Realty and Cushman & Wakefield brokered the $109.5 million sale of Tice's Corner, an Apple-anchored lifestyle retail destination in Woodcliff Lake, New Jersey, to WS Development. The asset changed hands from decades-long legacy ownership and ranks among New Jersey's largest single-asset retail transactions in a decade. The supply-constrained Bergen County market and strong national tenant mix underscore the property's institutional quality.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Retail-focused transaction in an affluent, supply-constrained suburban market may indicate strong consumer spending and wealth concentration that supports higher-end apartment rents nearby, but does not signal residential supply changes, zoning shifts, or employer growth that would inform multifamily strategy. Note as market strength indicator for suburban NJ only if Trammell Crow is developing luxury residential in Bergen County.

stories.title: 312-Unit Multifamily in Indiana Changes Hands
stories.excerpt: Northmarq’s Investment Sales team, led by Bobby Schiavone, Jordan Arand and Adam Klenk, led the sale of The Bend Apartments, a 312-unit garden apartment community located at 1909 Greentree Blvd. in Clarksville, Indiana.Northmarq represented the seller, a regional multifamily developer. The buyer was a private investor. “The Bend generated significant investor demand, further proving the depth of capital pursuing institutional-quality multifamily assets in the Louisville MSA where market fundamentals show consistent long-term growth,” said Schiavone. “ The property’s scale, vintage and strategic location made it an attractive opportunity for investors with long-term upside.” Built in 2023 and sitting on 13.22 acres, The Bend Apartments feature one-, two- and three-bedroom units.The Bend Apartments are conveniently located near shopping featuring national retailers, restaurants and the Green Tree Mall, as well as access to both Interstates 65 and 265. It is 10 minutes from River Ridge Commerce Center and downtown Louisville. The post 312-Unit Multifamily in Indiana Changes Hands appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: The Bend Apartments, 312-unit garden community in Clarksville, Indiana sold via Northmarq.
Louisville MSA asset shows 'significant investor demand' and 'institutional-quality' fundamentals.
Private investor buyer; seller was regional multifamily developer.
stories.summary: Northmarq facilitated the sale of The Bend Apartments, a 312-unit garden-style community in Clarksville, Indiana, from a regional developer to a private investor. The transaction generated robust investor interest, and the broker noted strong market fundamentals and long-term growth tailwinds in the Louisville MSA. No sale price disclosed.
stories.impact: Louisville MSA continues to attract institutional capital for stabilized multifamily assets, signaling healthy cap rates, solid fundamentals, and investor conviction in the market's trajectory. If Trammell Crow is underwriting new development or acquisitions in Louisville or Clarksville, this confirms the submarket's appeal and suggests competition may intensify for land and for lease-up. Monitor Louisville job growth (major employers, corporate expansion) and housing supply pipeline to assess entry timing.

stories.title: Weil, Gotshal’s Collapse Is Perfectly Timed for Manhattan’s Office Market
stories.excerpt: White-shoe law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges, which was founded in 1931 and announced its intent to wind down operations this week, currently occupies around 447,000 square feet over 11 floors at BXP’s General Motors Building at 767 Fifth Avenue. BXP owns 60 percent of the 50-story building, which it purchased in 2008 in a joint venture with Goldman Sachs and Meraas Capital. Weil Gotshal has called the building home since it opened in 1968, and last renewed its lease in 2014. The firm — which employed around 2,000 people including approximately 1,200 lawyers worldwide — was a pioneer in the field of bankruptcy and restructuring, having worked with the likes of Enron, Drexel Burnham Lambert, General Motors and Lehman Brothers, and one of the country’s 30 largest law firms as of just last year, bringing in nearly $2.1 billion in revenue. With the surprise announcement of the firm’s dissolution after a series of partner defections and the failure of a proposed merger with Willkie Farr & Gallagher, the future of its 447,000 square feet of Class A office space — for which the firm is committed until 2034 — is suddenly up in the air, leaving a potentially sizable hole in the otherwise booming and largely occupied Class A Manhattan office market. (Bloomberg reported that Weil associates and staff were told they would be paid for 90 days, and that a more detailed plan for the wind-down would be voted on within days. Weil also announced that it will continue serving clients during the wind-down period.) Manhattan’s office market has enjoyed a strong year, with Savills placing the borough’s leasing activity through the end of the third quarter at 33.5 million square feet, up 5.6 percent from the same time last year despite rapidly shrinking supply for Class A and trophy space. The company noted that legal services was one of the industry sectors driving the strong demand. Prominent leases from law firms in 2026 have included Simpson Thacher & Bartlett taking 916,000
bullets: Weil, Gotshal & Manges winds down; vacates 447k sq ft at BXP's GM Building, Manhattan.
Law firm occupied 11 floors at 767 Fifth Avenue since 1968; lease renewed 2014.
Dissolution follows partner departures and failed Willkie Farr & Gallagher merger; ~2,000 employees.
stories.summary: White-shoe law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges announced its wind-down after 94 years, vacating approximately 447,000 square feet across 11 floors at Boston Properties' General Motors Building (767 Fifth Avenue, Midtown Manhattan). The firm, which had occupied the space since the building opened in 1968, will leave one of Manhattan's most prestigious Class A office addresses as a result of partner defections and a failed merger attempt. The departure represents a significant loss of anchor tenancy for BXP.
stories.impact: Weil Gotshal's 447k-sq-ft departure from GM Building is a material negative for Manhattan office fundamentals and BXP's occupancy/cash flow, but a potential opportunity for multifamily indirectly: (1) massive back-office, professional-services job losses (~2,000 employees) could depress downtown residential demand near Fifth Avenue; (2) the extended vacancy may depress Midtown Manhattan's office market further, reducing corporate relocation tailwinds to NYC and slowing job-driven multifamily demand. If Trammell Crow is considering Manhattan residential near Midtown, factor in law-firm/professional-services sector weakness and potential workforce reductions as headwinds to leasing.

stories.title: Irvine Company Secures $157M Multifamily Refi in L.A.’s Playa Vista
stories.excerpt: Irvine Company has secured a $157.2 million refinancing loan from Capital One for a 309-unit luxury apartment property in Los Angeles’ Playa Vista neighborhood. The new Fannie Mae loan replaces a previous $136 million loan originated by PGIM, representing a roughly $21 million increase in financing, according to Yardi Matrix data cited by Multihousing News. The terms and maturity date of the new loan were not disclosed. The property, Villas at Playa Vista – Montecito, opened in 2016 at 12855 Runway Road. The community features one- and two-bedroom apartments averaging 1,113 square feet, along with a swimming pool, a fitness center, coworking space and conference rooms. Irvine Company acquired the land from Brookfield in 2015, and developed the building alongside two other apartment communities: the 703-unit Sausalito and the 491-unit Malibu. The three properties total 1,503 apartments. The communities are part of the larger, 460-acre Playa Vista master-planned development, which transformed land formerly occupied by Howard Hughes’ aerospace operations. The neighborhood now includes more than 6,000 apartments, approximately 3 million square feet of office space and more than 200,000 square feet of retail. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Irvine Company refi'd 309-unit Villas at Playa Vista–Montecito for $157.2M via Capital One.
Fannie Mae loan replaces prior $136M PGIM facility; ~$21M equity increase.
Opened 2016; averages 1,113 sq ft; part of 1,503-unit Playa Vista cluster.
stories.summary: Irvine Company secured a $157.2 million Fannie Mae refinance from Capital One for the Villas at Playa Vista–Montecito, a 309-unit luxury apartment community in Playa Vista, Los Angeles. The new loan replaces a prior $136 million PGIM facility, representing roughly $21 million in incremental financing. The 2016-delivered property is one of three sister communities (totaling 1,503 units) within Irvine's larger 460-acre Playa Vista master-planned development.
stories.impact: The refinance signals strong asset performance and Fannie Mae appetite for stabilized, luxury multifamily in Playa Vista, a tech-adjacent, supply-constrained West L.A. submarket. The $21M cash-out and premium pricing suggest sustained rental strength and investor confidence in LA market trajectory. For Trammell Crow, this validates Playa Vista's fundamentals and the viability of new development or acquisition there; however, the large existing pipeline (Irvine's 1,503 units) may compress new-project pricing and lease-up speed. Monitor tech employment (Google, Meta, Snap) and new supply in Playa Vista for entry-point clarity.

stories.title: Grassroots Analytics Doubles D.C. Footprint With 25K-SF Office Lease
stories.excerpt: Grassroots Analytics has signed a 24,692-square-foot office lease spanning three floors at Arch Square in Downtown Washington, D.C. The company will more than double its footprint in the city as it relocates to 803 Seventh Street NW, a mixed-use property owned by Swiss real estate investment foundation AFIAA. The transaction brings the building’s office component to 100 percent occupied. The lease terms and asking rent were not disclosed. Avison Young‘s Greg Tomasso and Macy Parana represented AFIAA in the lease. Sean Balile, Jake Payne and Whitney Huang of Clarity Tenant Representation represented Grassroots Analytics. “Achieving full occupancy is a meaningful milestone, particularly in today’s office market,” Tomasso said in a statement. “The lease not only strengthens Arch Square’s tenant roster but also demonstrates that demand exists for the right product in the right location.” The deal comes as D.C.’s office leasing market shows improvement. Leasing volume increased 21 percent in the third quarter compared to the same period last year, according to Avison Young. Despite reaching full office occupancy, Arch Square still has approximately 25,000 square feet of specialized space available. AFIAA is marketing the space to retailers and prospective tenants that might be considering creative offices, showrooms or other uses. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Grassroots Analytics leased 24,692 sq ft (3 floors) at Arch Square, downtown D.C.; 100% occupancy.
Tenant doubles D.C. footprint; mixed-use property owned by Swiss AFIAA foundation.
D.C. office leasing volume up 21% in Q3; demand for 'right product, right location.'
stories.summary: Grassroots Analytics signed a 24,692-square-foot office lease across three floors at Arch Square (803 Seventh Street NW), downtown Washington, D.C., more than doubling its footprint in the city. The transaction brought the building to 100% occupancy. Avison Young noted improved D.C. leasing activity (Q3 volume up 21%) and attributed the success to quality assets and premium locations.
stories.impact: While office-focused, the lease demonstrates D.C. office-market stabilization and tenant commitment to downtown core (near Metro, institutional anchors), which indirectly supports multifamily demand via proximity to jobs and amenities. Grassroots Analytics' expansion signals mid-market tech/analytics job growth in D.C., a historically government-sector-dependent market. If Trammell Crow is developing multifamily near downtown D.C. or Crystal City/Ballston, this confirms office-market recovery and ancillary employment growth; however, quantify the scale of Grassroots headcount to assess residential demand lift (likely modest, unless part of broader tech influx).

stories.title: Juda Chetrit Seals $55M Recap for 1384 Broadway
stories.excerpt: Juda Chetrit’s Chetrit Organization has secured a $55 million loan to recapitalize 1384 Broadway, Commercial Observer has learned. Maxim Capital Group provided the loan for the 80 percent occupied office building at Broadway and West 38th Street in Midtown Manhattan, sources familiar with the deal told CO. The transaction includes capital for lobby renovations, upgraded amenities and lease-up of the 204,034-square-foot tower. Iron Hound Management negotiated the recap. Iron Hound, Maxim and Chetrit declined to comment. Chetrit sealed the fresh capital for 1384 Broadway nearly a year after a previous $88 million commercial mortgage-backed securities loan, securitized in the CD 2017-CD3 conduit deal, hit special servicing in December 2025. The loan remained current as the borrower sought to finalize a discounted payoff before the end of 2026, according to David Putro, head of commercial real estate analytics at Morningstar Credit Analytics. That payoff is now completed. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Juda Chetrit recapped 1384 Broadway (Midtown Manhattan) with $55M loan from Maxim Capital.
80% occupied office tower; 204k sq ft; capital allocated to lobby reno, leasing.
Prior $88M CMBS loan entered special servicing Dec 2025; payoff completed via refi.
stories.summary: Juda Chetrit's Chetrit Organization secured a $55 million recapitalization loan from Maxim Capital Group for 1384 Broadway, an 80% occupied, 204,034-square-foot office tower in Midtown Manhattan at Broadway and West 38th Street. The fresh capital will fund lobby renovations, amenity upgrades, and lease-up efforts. The deal resolves a prior $88 million CMBS loan that entered special servicing in December 2025, with the borrower now executing a discounted payoff and recapitalization strategy.
stories.impact: Another Manhattan office refi/distress-resolution signal: the prior CMBS loan's special-servicing status indicated stress, and the discounted payoff + recap structure suggest Midtown office cap-rate compression and valuation challenges. While the refi secures near-term liquidity, 1384 Broadway's ongoing 20% vacancy and reliance on capital-markets support indicate persistent Manhattan office headwinds. For multifamily, this reinforces that Manhattan office weakness (job losses, reduced corporate density) will suppress residential demand growth. Avoid aggressive pricing assumptions for new Manhattan multifamily projects until office-market trajectory clarifies.
